criticisms.target: The formula n_eff versus the headline 2.18 and the 0.67 cited in Why they agree
criticisms.criticism: The article's own formula with n=9 and r 0.67 yields n_eff 1.42 and 1.74 even at the cross-family 0.53, not 2.18, so the two load-bearing numbers in the piece are mutually inconsistent.

criticisms.target: The claim in The honest half that near-tie invisibility is the real problem versus what the toolbox returns
criticisms.criticism: The piece names the inability to identify which decisions were near-ties as the core problem then ships a tool that reports n_eff, echo count and solo findings, none of which identify near-ties.

criticisms.target: The instruction to run the nine checks and one of them twice versus judges six through nine adding 0.22
criticisms.criticism: The prescribed protocol spends ten runs after the article has demonstrated that nothing beyond the fifth judge buys measurable independence, contradicting its own evidence.

criticisms.target: The three framing instructions specifically argue-the-opposite
criticisms.criticism: A reviewer instructed to argue the opposite disagrees by construction, mechanically depressing r and inflating n_eff without adding genuine independent judgment, so the protocol games the metric it reports.

criticisms.target: The sentence Two frontier labs three weeks apart publishing that their checks were correlated with the thing being checked
criticisms.criticism: Neither cited incident shows correlation between checker and checked, the Anthropic case is monitor evasion and the OpenAI case is monitors that existed but were never applied, so the conclusion does not follow from its evidence.

criticisms.target: On the decisions that were nearly tied it is worth 10 to 23 points
criticisms.criticism: The unit is never defined and no explanation is given for how a 10 to 23 point effect on a subset averages to almost exactly nothing overall.

criticisms.target: On this evidence agreement is the one thing that should not raise your confidence
criticisms.criticism: This contradicts the article's own honest half concession that correlated checks pay 10 to 23 points on near-ties and ignores that agreement among independent reviewers is informative.

criticisms.target: The OpenAI claim in Two labs said the same thing this month versus its entry in Sources
criticisms.criticism: The body says OpenAI disclosed a system left its sandbox and reached production while the source note attributes it to TIME reporting about a paused training run, a mismatch in attribution and in what happened.

criticisms.target: Measured it was worth about a fifth of what you thought you were buying
criticisms.criticism: The article's own formula gives a second check n_eff 1.44, so the second opinion delivers about 44 per cent of a fresh opinion not a fifth, and the fifth is the whole-panel dilution wrongly applied to the marginal second check.

criticisms.target: The prescribed second axis three instructions neutral reviewer find-the-error and argue-the-opposite
criticisms.criticism: Two of the three framings are deliberately adversarial instructions so the disagreement they produce is manufactured by the prompt rather than evidence of independent judgement, and crossing them into r systematically inflates n_eff.

criticisms.target: r is how much they agreed with each other, never agree and n_eff is n
criticisms.criticism: The design-effect formula requires a correlation coefficient not an agreement rate, and with a verdict drawn from a fixed four-item list chance agreement alone is about 25 per cent, so the stated procedure computes the wrong quantity.

criticisms.target: Two frontier labs three weeks apart publishing that their checks were correlated with the thing being checked
criticisms.criticism: Neither cited incident is a correlation result, obfuscation defeating a monitor is evasion and OpenAI having built monitors it never applied is a deployment failure, so the evidence does not support the claim.

criticisms.target: The headline figure 2.18 and its sources-line caveat
criticisms.criticism: The sources note concedes the study ran on natural-language-inference and reward benchmarks rather than open-ended review yet the article and the tool apply 2.18 to open-ended document review, the domain the caveat excludes.

criticisms.target: measured across families the correlation falls by about 0.13 from roughly 0.67 to 0.53
criticisms.criticism: These correlations are irreconcilable with the headline, a nine-model panel at 0.53 yields n_eff 1.72 not 2.18, and 0.67 to 0.53 is a fall of 0.14 not 0.13.

criticisms.target: Nothing is stored and nothing is sent anywhere in the toolbox section
criticisms.criticism: The procedure requires running nine checks in whatever assistant you already have which sends the reviewed document to third-party model providers, so the privacy claim is false as written.

criticisms.target: A panel of humans reviewing the same work scores 4.0 to 5.8 on the same measure
criticisms.criticism: n_eff is bounded by and scales with panel size so quoting a human range without stating how many humans were on those panels makes the comparison with the nine-model 2.18 uninterpretable.

criticisms.target: The n_eff formula in The test
criticisms.criticism: The design effect discounts a sample used to estimate a mean whereas review is a union-coverage problem where a correlated reviewer who surfaces one defect nobody else surfaced has delivered full value, so the work must show n_eff predicts defects-found.

criticisms.target: The 0.22 marginal-independence claim set against read the solo findings
criticisms.criticism: The piece declares judges six through nine worthless then names solo findings as the entire return on running more than one, which is the output those marginal judges disproportionately produce.

criticisms.target: The 2.18 figure alongside the 0.67 to 0.53 correlation range
criticisms.criticism: n_eff of 2.18 across nine judges implies a mean pairwise correlation of about 0.39 which is below the cross-family 0.53 cited as best case, so the two headline numbers cannot both describe the same kind of panel.

criticisms.target: You get a fifth of the way there
criticisms.criticism: Moving r from 0.67 to 0.53 raises n_eff on nine checks from about 1.42 to 1.72, a 21 per cent gain in effective opinions, which the piece dismisses by measuring the drop on a linear scale to zero that its own formula says is not the operative one.

criticisms.target: The near-tie result worth 10 to 23 points
criticisms.criticism: If the payoff is real concentrated and unidentifiable in advance and a full panel costs pennies then the expected-value conclusion is to keep running second checks on everything rather than stop trusting them.

criticisms.target: Human disagreement is not noise it is the product
criticisms.criticism: This asserts without evidence that the human 4.0 to 5.8 baseline reflects genuine independent signal rather than inattention and rater noise, and the benchmark collapses if human n_eff is high simply because humans are less reliable.

criticisms.target: The Anthropic and OpenAI section
criticisms.criticism: A model evading its own monitors and an unreleased system leaving a sandbox are adversarial-evasion failures by the system under test not correlated judgment among independent reviewers, and a detection range of 1 to 60 per cent carries no information.

criticisms.target: Nothing is stored and nothing is sent anywhere
criticisms.criticism: A procedure whose first step is running your document through nine model configurations necessarily transmits that document to whatever assistant or API serves them so this privacy claim is false as written.

criticisms.target: The 0.67 to 0.53 correlation figures in Why they agree set against the 2.18 headline
criticisms.criticism: A nine-model panel with pairwise correlations of 0.53 to 0.67 yields n_eff of about 1.7 by the article's own formula not 2.18, so the two headline numbers cannot both describe the same panel.

criticisms.target: Measured it was worth about a fifth of what you thought you were buying
criticisms.criticism: The fifth is silently imported from the cross-family correlation drop whereas the article's own equation makes a second check worth roughly 44 per cent of a fresh opinion, so the opening number contradicts the method the piece prescribes.

criticisms.target: A panel of humans reviewing the same work scores 4.0 to 5.8 on the same measure
criticisms.criticism: The human panel size is never stated so a raw n_eff of 4.0 to 5.8 cannot be compared with 2.18 out of nine without knowing whether the humans were nine twelve or a hundred.

criticisms.target: On the decisions that were nearly tied it is worth 10 to 23 points
criticisms.criticism: The unit of points is never defined and the near-tie base rate is never given so the claim that the overall effect is almost exactly nothing cannot be reconciled with a 10 to 23 point gain.

criticisms.target: Two frontier labs three weeks apart publishing that their checks were correlated with the thing being checked
criticisms.criticism: Neither cited incident is about correlated judges, obfuscation defeating a monitor is adversarial evasion and OpenAI not applying monitors it had built is a process failure, so the section equivocates on correlated.

criticisms.target: Nothing is stored and nothing is sent anywhere in What comes back
criticisms.criticism: A procedure that runs ten checks across three model families necessarily sends the document to those providers so the privacy claim is false as written for the tool's own default path.

criticisms.target: The toolbox procedure run the nine checks and one of them twice
criticisms.criticism: The article establishes that judges six through nine add 0.22 between them then prescribes a nine-check protocol whose last four checks its own finding says are near-worthless.

criticisms.target: The formula applied to the prescribed three by three design
criticisms.criticism: The formula assumes one exchangeable correlation among comparable numeric scores yet the recommended output is a categorical verdict plus one-line criticisms from a block-structured grid, and the piece never says how r is computed from that.
